sub_indicators.label: People who use the internet
sub_indicators.subject: infra.connect
sub_indicators.text: Internet usage: people who use the internet
sub_indicators.norm_short: The African Union's Agenda 2063 plan asks that broadband reach 80 per cent of the population by 2033. The International Telecommunication Union's 2030 target is that everyone aged 15 and over uses the internet.
criteria: The latest figure, for 2024 or later, shows fewer than a quarter of the population using the internet.

At least a quarter of the population uses the internet: 25 per cent or more in the latest figure, for 2024 or later. A national survey, census or government figure for a share of people is used where one is held, otherwise the International Telecommunication Union's estimate.
At least half use it: 50 per cent or more.
At least four in five use it: 80 per cent or more.
Nearly everyone uses it: 95 per cent or more. Counts of subscriptions, regulators' and operators' user counts, and figures for adults only, are never used at any stage.
